goal: Authenticated users can operate the existing personal preferences, Secrets, Registries, CLI/API token, and optional Agents routes while guests, CLI clients, and unknown routes receive resilient prototype-aligned login, authorization, and not-found states.
non_goals: Do not add routes, APIs, typed fields, stores, backend behavior, persistence, dependencies, migrations, authentication algorithms, callback protocol fields, or prototype fixtures.

Do not implement password or SSO login, profile updates, avatar sync, notifications, token one-time semantics, authorized apps, device or location approval, Agent telemetry, or unsupported personal endpoints.
Do not implement baseline task 5.4 permission-family closure, task 5.5 full parity closure, verified row statuses, or complete A2.
expected_evidence: Focused router and component tests covering all eight destinations, current metadata, responsive personal navigation, feature disablement, explicit states, current mutations, and 390px containment.
Deferred-response regressions proving personal list, editor, token, login, and CLI callback completions belong to the active lifecycle and cannot lock or overwrite successor state.
Full frontend Vitest, targeted Prettier, ESLint, TypeScript, Vite build, syntax, JSON/JSONL, diff checks, and exact 32-state task-local browser evidence.
Evidence-bearing task report and independent spec/quality reviews that verify task-scoped A3/A4 only and keep task 5.5 and complete A2 open.
unsafe_assumptions: Prototype hierarchy does not authorize unsupported profile, login, token, application, callback, or Agent capabilities.
Personal resource labels do not replace the current organization API contract based on user.org_id.
A numeric callback query is unsafe until strict decimal port validation succeeds.
Representative task evidence does not establish complete permission, theme, locale, and data-state parity.
stop_condition: Stop if implementation needs files outside the locked task scope, a new route/API/type/store/backend/dependency/authentication/migration/callback contract, prototype-only data or actions, token exposure, or task 5.4/5.5 family-wide closure.
